capabilities.target: executive's drive (board materials, draft financial results)
any recipient, sent from the executive's mailbox

inputs.source: Calendar invites, including from outside the company; free-text description authored by the sender

instructions.note: The instruction to 'find related documents' and 'email a short brief to the attendees' places no limit on which documents may be searched or who may receive them, so whoever sends the invite effectively controls both the search scope and the recipient list.

'Related documents' is not defined relative to the meeting's sensitivity or the invite's source trust, so the agent has no stated basis to exclude confidential board or financial materials from a search triggered by an external invite.

'Manage the executive's calendar' and 'act on invites as they arrive' imply standing authority to accept any invite and correspond under the executive's identity, with no instruction distinguishing trusted internal invites from untrusted external ones.

elements.name: Agent-authored daily summary reviewed by the executive
Executive's drive (board materials, draft financial results)

controls.name: Block external send of confidential/restricted data
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by a classification/DLP check outside the model at the mail gateway; it blocks the send regardless of model behavior, so it does not decay with model capability, though its owner could disable it (control_removal).

controls.name: Human approval before sending externally
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action gate reviewed by a human before every external send does not decay with model capability, though it would weaken under high volume or if the gate were removed.

controls.name: Spotlight invite content as untrusted
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model treating the invite's free-text description as data rather than instruction; a more capable or adversarially prompted model is more likely to rationalize following it.

controls.name: Rate limit on invite-triggered actions
controls.decay_rationale: A hard cap on invite-triggered reads/sends per unit time, enforced outside the model, does not decay with model capability, though it only narrows rather than closes the path and can be removed by its owner.

controls.name: Independent, tamper-evident action log
controls.decay_rationale: A log written by the orchestration layer rather than by the model itself cannot be selectively omitted by the agent, so it does not decay with model capability.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted calendar invite drives confidential drive read and external email send

attack_path.note: Anyone can send the executive an invite with attacker-authored free-text description.
Agent searches the executive's drive, including board materials and draft financial results, to prepare the brief.
Agent emails the brief, including whatever was found, to the invite's attendees — which include the external sender.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Any new integration that adds further egress capability from the executive's mailbox or drive, or any widening of drive_read scope to other confidential repositories.

evidence.observation: Agent accepts invites and emails a brief with related documents to attendees for every new invite, with no distinction between internal and external senders.

Anyone can send the executive a calendar invite with a free-text description; mail.send has no recipient restrictions and no approval step; the drive holds confidential board materials and draft financial results.

recommendations.action: Block mail.send from transmitting confidential- or restricted-classified content to any recipient outside the organization's verified domain, enforced at the mail gateway, not by the model.
Require raw-action human approval before mail.send fires for any invite-triggered brief addressed to an external recipient.
Treat invite descriptions as untrusted content: spotlight/delimit them and never let them steer which documents are retrieved or who receives the brief.
Log and flag every drive_read followed by a mail_send to a recipient outside the organization for review.

findings.title: No independent record of agent actions: the daily review summary is self-authored

forecast.watch_signal: Autonomy raised from A3 (act then report) to A4 (fully autonomous) without adding an independent audit log, removing even the current self-reported daily check.

evidence.observation: The daily summary is written by the agent itself, so there is no independent, tamper-evident record of what actions were taken that the executive could use to catch errors or manipulation.

recommendations.action: Generate the daily summary, or a parallel audit trail, from an independent log written by the orchestration layer rather than from the agent's own narrative, so the executive can verify what actually happened.

findings.title: No rate or step limit on invite-triggered actions

forecast.watch_signal: Median invites processed per day rising, or max_unattended_steps/max_runtime_minutes remaining unset as the agent takes on higher step-volume tasks.

evidence.observation: 'Act on invites as they arrive' states no volume limit, and autonomy.max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes are both unset, so an attacker who sends many invites can trigger unlimited drive reads and mail sends.
Anyone can send the executive a calendar invite, and mail.send has no recipient restrictions and no approval step, so there is no gate to slow a flood of invite-triggered actions.

recommendations.action: Impose a hard rate limit or step cap on invite-triggered drive reads and mail sends per unit time, and route bursts to a human queue instead of auto-processing them.

stride_coverage.rationale: The agent process runs within the organization's trusted infrastructure and is not itself an impersonable network identity in this design; the relevant spoofing risk is the untrusted invite sender, covered under ext.invite_sender.
autonomy.can_modify_own_config is false and the design describes no mechanism by which an external party could alter the agent's own process or configuration.
This is an inbound flow carrying attacker-authored invite text into the agent; it does not carry organizational data outward, so outbound disclosure is covered by the flow.mail_send element instead.
mail.send transmits over the organization's authenticated mail infrastructure; the risk in this design is what content is sent and to whom, not alteration of the message in transit.
The daily summary is shown only to the executive, who already has full access to every underlying document and message it references, so it exposes no new party.
The daily summary is a simple internal report with no described dependency or capacity limit that an attacker could exhaust through this store.
cap.drive_read is read-only; the design grants the agent no write capability against the drive, so this path cannot alter stored documents.
The calendar platform independently records the sending account for each invite; attributing the external sender is a property of that platform, not a gap this agent's design introduces.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical: an untrusted calendar invite can drive the agent to read the executive's confidential board and financial documents and email them to the invite's own external attendees (the lethal trifecta), with no distinction made between trusted and untrusted triggers. No structural or even meaningful behavioral controls are declared anywhere in the design: mail.send has no recipient restriction or approval step, and the only instruction governing document search and sending is a bare task description, which the rubric does not credit as a control, so residual risk remains critical. Two property findings round out the picture: the daily summary meant to catch problems is self-authored with no independent, tamper-evident record (repudiation, high), and there is no rate or step limit on invite-triggered actions, so a flood of invites could multiply the damage or exhaust resources (high). Forecast risk stays at the residual ceiling; because no control currently constrains the path, no additional trigger is needed to reach critical, and future changes such as new egress-capable tools, wider data scope, or higher autonomy would only entrench it further.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No MCP config, tool manifest, or IaC was provided; the exact mechanics of mail.send and drive.search_and_read are inferred from the narrative description, which limits confidence on implementation detail to medium even though the design gaps themselves are stated explicitly.
The volume of calendar invites and the executive's daily review process are not quantified in the artifacts, which limits precision on approval-fatigue and denial-of-service likelihood estimates.
